title: Model eval tooling patterns: loaders, scoring, and CI checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures pragmatic patterns and minimal runnable examples for the evals harness we use to onboard new model variants into Redwood's serving fleet. Focus areas: small reproducible scripts, dataset loader conventions, canonical scoring helpers, and the CI gating workflow that prevents regressions from reaching production.

Audience and scope:
- Audience: applied-ml engineers, SREs who run eval CI, and solutions engineers triaging quality regressions.
- Not in scope: deep research metric design (we link to the separate metrics catalog), nor heavy-weight human eval UX.

High-level architecture (how pieces fit together):
- eval-runner (python CLI): orchestrates dataset ingestion -> prompt templating -> model inference (via local adapter or API) -> scoring -> artifact write.
- loaders/ (package): small loader functions that return a standardized list[dict] with keys: id, input, target (optional), metadata.
- prompts/ templates: plain-text templates with {input} placeholders and optional instruction variants.
- scoring/ utils: deterministic comparators (exact match, token-overlap), and probabilistic/regression-aware hooks (safety flags, hallucination heuristics).
- ci/ (github actions): lightweight job that runs on model version bumps or PRs touching evals/ or model catalog entries.

Design goals and constraints:
- reproducible: small docker image + pinned python deps (requirements-evals.txt).
- fast feedback: smoke tests complete <10 min for quick PR gating.
- noisy but actionable: fail CI only on clear regressions (delta + threshold + sample inspection).
- auditable artifacts: store raw outputs, scores, and a short human-friendly summary (CSV + JSON + plain-text report).

Filesystem layout (recommended):
- evals/
  - runners/cli.py  # thin wrapper to call orchestration
  - loaders/
    - common_csv.py
    - hf_jsonl.py
    - synthetic_generators.py
  - prompts/
    - classification/intent_prompts.md
    - summarization/summary_templates.md
  - scoring/
    - metrics.py
    - heuristics.py
  - ci/
    - gh_actions_smoke.yaml
  - examples/
    - smoke_runs/

Loader pattern (minimal contract):
- every loader must expose: load(path_or_ref) -> list_of_examples
- example schema (dict): id (str), input (str), target (str | null), meta (dict)
- loaders should be defensive: convert encodings to utf-8, remove control chars, validate text length distribution and return a small sample for quick checks.

Example loader (conceptual, not full code):
- hf_jsonl loader:
  - accepts: s3:// or local path to jsonl where each line is {"id":..., "input":..., "target":..., "lang":...}
  - on load: apply language filter, drop rows with missing input, add meta.source = filename, return first N for smoke.

Prompt templating rules:
- Use simple python .format style with explicit escape for braces. Keep templates under 2 sentences for smoke tests.
- Maintain two versions: canonical (for stable baselines) and exploratory (for new instructions).
- Store per-task prompt variants with names and short descriptions (why this probe matters).

Scoring functions and heuristics (patterns):
- deterministic scoring: exact_match (normalized), token_f1 (whitespace tokenization), normalized_edit_distance (Levenshtein / max_len).
- prob-based scoring: logprob of target generation when we can get token probs; use for calibration/regression on top-k quality.
- safety/sanity heuristics: hallucination_score = ratio_of_entities_not_in_input, repetition_rate, off-topic_detector (embedding similarity between input and generation).
- composite score: weighted combination; default weights: 0.6 semantic (embed sim), 0.3 token_f1, 0.1 safety_penalty.

Regression detection policy (CI gating):
- define a control baseline model (pin model id + dataset + prompt seed).
- run N runs (N_small=200 for smoke, N_full=2000 nightly).
- compute per-metric delta: new_score - baseline_score.
- fail criteria: if delta < -delta_threshold for primary metric AND p_value < 0.05 (bootstrap). For smoke: require larger delta_threshold.
- when CI fails: produce artifacts: failing_examples.csv (top 10 worst by delta), full_runs.jsonl, summary.md with suggested next steps.

CI wiring (practical checklist and sample flow):
- trigger: PR touches evals/ OR model catalog (models.yaml) OR model onboarding metadata.
- job matrix: quick-smoke (200 examples, single small token cap), optional full-nightly (scheduled).
- runner environment: uses GH Actions with self-hosted runners on medium GPU (if model needs local run) OR mocks via hosted API token for hosted runs.
- caching: cache dataset samples by sha to avoid re-fetching large datasets.
- artifact storage: upload artifacts to S3 under s3://redwood-evals-artifacts/{pr}/{run_ts}/.

Sample GH Actions snippets (described):
- jobs:
  - smoke-eval:
      runs-on: self-hosted
      steps:
        - checkout
        - setup python (3.10)
        - install requirements-evals.txt
        - run: python -m evals.runners.cli --loader path/to/sample.jsonl --model-ref PR_CANDIDATE --smoke 200 --out s3://...
        - upload-artifact: failing_examples.csv, summary.md

Human-in-the-loop review patterns:
- if CI flags a regression, auto-post a comment on PR with a short summary and link to artifacts. Include a toggle to request SME review.
- maintain a stale-pr policy: if a model PR stays failing >2 weeks without owner action, auto-close and notify product owner.

Checklist for onboarding a new model variant (developer flow):
- [ ] Add a model entry to models.yaml with required fields: name, id, hardware_reqs, quantized_variants.
- [ ] Add/choose dataset loader(s) and mark canonical dataset(s) for the model.
- [ ] Create a smoke eval config under evals/examples/smoke_configs/ referencing the loader + prompt + metrics.
- [ ] Run locally: python -m evals.runners.cli --config smoke_configs/your.yaml --local 
- [ ] Open PR and ensure CI smoke run completes. Attach failing_examples if any.

Diagnostics and debugging tips (common gotchas):
- mismatched tokenization: ensure loader normalization and model tokenizer agree. Add a pre-check script that tokenizes both target and predicted text and reports avg token count ratio.
- flakiness: seed RNG and log seeds, stash deterministic torch/transformers seeds in the run metadata.
- long-tail failures: include a 'context length' histogram in the report to spot distribution drift.
- differing model interfaces: wrap remote API calls behind an adapter class with same response contract for local model class.

Artifacts we keep per run:
- run_manifest.json (metadata: model_ref, commit_hash, env, seed)
- outputs.jsonl (id, input, generation, raw_probs?, meta)
- scoring.csv (id, metric1, metric2, composite_score)
- failing_examples.csv (top K by metric delta)
- summary.md (human summary with graphs inline as image links)

Minimal reproducible smoke example (conceptual):
- files to touch: evals/examples/smoke_configs/qa_smoke.yaml, a loader that returns 200 QA pairs, one prompt template under prompts/qa/, metrics configured to use token_f1 and embed-sim.
- run: python -m evals.runners.cli --config qa_smoke.yaml --smoke 200 --model-ref local:checkpoint-2024-09

Open questions and TODOs (notes to self):
- unify the composite score weights across teams (product prefers embed-sim heavy, infra worries about token-level regressions). Proposal: expose weightset per product area and record which weightset was used in run_manifest.
- better tooling around partial-run replays (replay only failing ids against a candidate patch).
- evaluate if bootstrap p-value approach is too strict for small smokes; explore bayesian decision rules.

References and related docs:
- metrics catalog (confluence link in linked_artifacts)
- onboarding checklist (product playbook)
- current GH Actions templates: infra/ci/evals/gh_actions_templates

Quick notes (informal):
- \"notes to future me\": rely on the run_manifest heavily; if something goes wrong the manifest is the fastest explanation.
- keep smoke datasets tiny but representative; avoid copying entire evaluation corpora for quick PRs.
- when in doubt prefer deterministic, explainable heuristics over opaque black-box signals in CI gating.

If you want, I can produce the concrete CLI script and a small example loader (jsonl -> examples) in the repo as a follow-up PR.
